QASHANI:107:7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:107:7/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:107:7/r1.claim: The woe concerns people whose prayer lacks presence and sincerity; calling them “prayers” indicts them because even their finest outward deed becomes sin without those conditions.
QASHANI:107:7/r1.anchor: إن صلوا غفلوا عن صلاتهم لاحتجابهم عن حقيقتها بجهلهم وعدم حضورهم

QASHANI:107:7/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:107:7/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:107:7/r2.claim: The plural form addresses a class, since the denier of judgment is treated as a generic type.
QASHANI:107:7/r2.anchor: وأورد على صيغة الجمع لأن المراد بالذي يكذب هو الجنس

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r4.claim: The custodians appear to pray, but their prayers lack spirit and devotion and are pretentious; insincerity toward God also makes a person a poor neighbour to others.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r4.anchor: their prayers lack spirit and devotion and are in fact a show of pretence on their part

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r5.claim: The custodians' public display of worship cannot instil true worship and amounts to fooling the public.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r5.anchor: but a matter of fooling the public

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r6.claim: The House's real purpose was to establish prayer; Abraham settled Ishmael nearby so his descendants could maintain worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r6.anchor: the real purpose for which the Baytull āh was built was the establishment of the prayer

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r7.claim: Abraham prayed for peace and sustenance in the land for the sake of establishing prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r7.anchor: His humble invocation to the Almighty is cited in the Qur’ ān as follows

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r8.claim: The Qur’an testifies that Ishmael enjoined prayer and zakāh on his people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p472/r8.anchor: How Ishmael (sws) fulfilled this obligation, the Qur’ ān itself testifies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r1.claim: Prayer and zakāh persisted even when sorcerers and innovators held sway, but both institutions were distorted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r1.anchor: the institutions of prayer and zak āh continued, though they became completely distorted and disfigured

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r2.claim: The Qur’an says the prayer at the House had become whistling and clapping.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r2.anchor: Their prayer at the Baytull āh is nothing but whistling and clapping of hands

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r3.claim: Quraysh leaders upheld these rituals on special occasions, just as leaders elsewhere feigned austerity through displays of religiosity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r3.anchor: the leaders of the Quraysh too on special occasions upheld these practices

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r4.claim: The verse warns people who do not know prayer's true essence and rebukes their unworthiness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r4.anchor: This verse actually upbraids such unworthy persons as are unawar e of the real essence of the prayer

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r6.speaker: Some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r6.claim: Some infer that the sūrah is Medinan because it condemns people who pray ostentatiously, whom they think could not have existed in Makkah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r6.anchor: They contend that such people who used to pretend righteousness could not have existed in Makkah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r7.claim: The Medinan dating is mistaken because the prayer here is the earlier institution commanded to Ishmael and his descendants with the building of the House; it persisted later in a distorted form.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r7.anchor: prayer whose establishment had bee n ordained by the Almighty to the prophet Ishmael

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r10.claim: After naming denial of judgment as the root of unbelief, the passage turns to prayer as worship owed to the Creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r10.anchor: ولما ذكر أولا عمود الكفر، وهو التكذيب بالدين، ذكر ما يترتب عليه مما يتعلق بالخالق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r11.claim: The apparent reading makes those praying a separate group; another view identifies them as the orphan-abuser who also fails to urge feeding. The author's likelier explanation is hypocrites who perform prayer outwardly without Muslim belief or devotion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن المصلين هم غير المذكور. وقيل: هو داع اليتيم غير الحاض،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers an alternative syntax joining fa-dhālika to the one who denies judgment, omitting the answer to araʾayta, and making the woe to praying hypocrites a description standing for their pronoun; generic singular carries a plural sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.anchor: وطريقة أخرى أن يكون فذلك عطفا على الذي يكذب، إما عطف ذات على ذات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhsharī's accusative parsing of fa-dhālika strange and unnatural: a nominative subject is immediate, while an accusative would require repeating the verb and pointing needlessly to the person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.anchor: فجعل فذلك في موضع نصب عطفا على المفعول، وهو تركيب غريب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r4.claim: He calls it an evident strain to replace a pronoun with al-muṣallīn and treat the plural as required because the referent of alladhī yukadhdhib is collective; Qurʾān should follow the apparent syntax.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r4.anchor: وأن المصلين جمع، لأن ضمير الذي يكذب معناه الجمع، فتكلف واضح ولا ينبغي أن يحمل القرآن إلا على ما اقتضاه ظاهر التركيب

FARRA:v3p294#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p294#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v3p294#2/r4.claim: The threatened worshippers are hypocrites who are heedless or lax about prayer; Ibn ʿAbbās gives this interpretation, also found in ʿAbd Allāh's reading.
FARRA:v3p294#2/r4.anchor: فويل للمصلين (4) يعني: المنافقين «الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون» يقول: لاهون كذلك فسرها ابن عباس،

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.claim: The fa in the woe passage is consequential: neglect of the orphan already shows weak religion and deserves blame, so heedlessness of prayer, ostentation, and withholding zakāt merit it even more; prayer is religion's pillar, ostentation a branch of unbelief, and zakāt Islam's bridge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4.anchor: فالسهو عن الصلاة التي هي عماد الدين والرياء الذي هو شعبة من الكفر، ومنع الزكاة التي هي قنطرة الإسلام أحق بذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r5.claim: Alternatively, the fa can mark causation, meaning, “So woe is theirs.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r5.anchor: أو للسببية على معنى { فويل } لهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.claim: Calling them “those who pray” in place of a pronoun signals their bad treatment of both the Creator and other people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6.anchor: وإنما وضع المصلين موضع الضمير للدلالة على سوء معاملتهم مع الخالق والخلق

BINTSHATI:v2p191/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r3.claim: The warned worshippers do perform prayer, but are heedless of standing before the Creator and of prayer's power to curb arrogance and cultivate humility and conscience.
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r3.anchor: قد أثبت أنهم فعلاً يؤدون الصلاة، ولكنهم ساهون عن صلاتهم غافلون عن كونها قياماً بين يدى الخالق

BINTSHATI:v2p191/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r4.claim: A prayer that leaves its worshipper indifferent to an orphan's needs or a poor person's right to food cannot come from a humble, believing heart; it becomes a show for gain or protection.
BINTSHATI:v2p191/r4.anchor: وصلاة الذي يدع اليتيم ولا يحض على طعام المسكين، لا يمكن أن تقام عن قلب خاشع وضمير مؤمن

BINTSHATI:v2p192/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r1.claim: The offering teaches that God receives piety, not animal meat or blood; the verse makes inward God-consciousness decisive.
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r1.anchor: وفي آية الحج: {لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم} 37.

BINTSHATI:v2p192/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r2.claim: The verse on righteousness joins prayer and zakat with keeping promises and patience, showing that virtue includes lived faith and care.
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r2.anchor: الصلاة وآتى الزكاة والموفون بعهدهم إذا عاهدوا والصابرين في البأساء والضراء

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، عكرمة، قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Ikrima, and Qatada classify the seven-verse sura as Meccan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.anchor: قيل: مكية، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.speaker: الضحاك، الواقدي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Waqidi classify the sura as Medinan.

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.claim: Muqatil says it is Meccan through the mention of the needy, with the remainder Medinan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.anchor: مكية إلى قوله: (المسكين) وباقي السورة مدنية، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.claim: A report transmitted from Ubayy says reciting this sura brings God's forgiveness for one who pays zakat; no grading is given.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (أرأيت) غفر الله له

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.claim: After recounting favors to Quraysh, the sura marvels at their conduct despite Meccan security and provision, then their denial of the Prophet and his prophethood.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.anchor: افتتح هذه السورة تعجبا من حالهم مع عظم النعم عليهم بمكة من الأمن والرزق

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r15.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r15.claim: Al-Hasan says the prayer warning describes a hypocrite who seeks no reward when praying on time and fears no penalty when praying late.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r15.anchor: أحدهما : أنه المنافق , إن صلاها لوقتها لم يرج ثوابها , وإن صلاها لغير وقتها لم يخش عقابها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r16.claim: The warning can be read as an ellipsis whose continuation is the following description, those who are heedless of prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r16.anchor: أن إضماره ظاهر متصل به , وهو قوله تعالى : { الذين هم } الآية .

MUQATIL:107:1-7/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r5.claim: The threatened worshipers in this verse are hypocrites.
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r5.anchor: { فويل للمصلين } [آية: 4] يعني المنافقين في هذه الآية

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Māʿūn an early Makkan sūrah after al-Takāthur, though some assign vv. 4–7 to Madinah; since the whole sūrah addresses religious hypocrisy, it may all be Madinan, when hypocrisy could gain political advantage.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.anchor: commentators maintain that al-Māʿūn is an early Makkan sūrah

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.claim: Religious hypocrisy is not treated as limited to Muslims alone.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.anchor: Nonetheless, hypocrisy in religion was not seen as limited to Muslims alone.

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed in the mission's early years, probably after surah 102; its title comes from al-ma'un in the last verse.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.anchor: revealed in the early years of the Prophet's mission (probably after surah 102), is derived from the word al-ma'un occurring in the last verse

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.speaker: some commentators
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.claim: Some commentators date verses 4–7 to Medina, but Asad rejects this view for lack of historical or textual evidence.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r2.anchor: The view of some commentators that verses 4-7 were revealed at Medina lacks all historical or textual evidence and may, therefore, be disregarded.

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.claim: The second section opens with the emphatic wail that introduces a catalogue of vices.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r1.anchor: einen rhetorisch markanten Einsatzpunkt auf, nämlich die einen Lasterkatalog einleitende Interjektion „Wehe …“ (wail)

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.claim: Verses 4–6 target the criticized people's neglect of ritual prayer.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die anschließenden Verse zielen zunächst (V. 4–6) auf die kultische Nachlässigkeit der Getadelten ab

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.claim: The two groups cross-correspond: verse 1 and verses 4–6 concern religious omissions, while verses 2–3 and verse 7 concern social omissions; the first group stresses social failings and the second religious ones.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.anchor: Inhaltlich korrespondieren insofern V. 1 und V. 4–6 (religiöse Unterlassungen) und V. 2.3 und V. 7 (soziale Unterlassungen)

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.claim: The surah warns people professing religion whose traits resemble hypocrites: neglecting prayer, acting ostentatiously, and withholding aid, all incompatible with belief in requital.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.anchor: بيان وعيد لمن كان من المنتحلين بالدين متخلقا بأخلاق المنافقين

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.claim: The surah may be Meccan or Medinan; another view says its first half is Meccan and second half Medinan.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية، وقيل نصفها مكي ونصفها مدني

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r10.claim: Those heedless of prayer do not care if they miss it entirely, miss some prayers, or delay it beyond its preferred time.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r10.anchor: أي غافلون لا يهتمون بها ولا يبالون أن تفوتهم بالكلية أو بعض الأوقات

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.claim: The consequence-marker applies the denier of requital to these praying people; they display belief while practically denying requital, so they are not free of hypocrisy.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.anchor: وفي الآية تطبيق من يكذب بالدين على هؤلاء المصلين لمكان فاء التفريع

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r16.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r16.claim: A report from Ali says prayer is God's most beloved deed, worldly matters must not distract from its times, and the condemned are heedless and treat prayer times lightly.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r16.anchor: ليس عمل أحب إلى الله عز وجل من الصلاة فلا يشغلنكم عن أوقاتها شيء من أمور الدنيا

THALABI:v10p305/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r1.speaker: عطاء بن دينار
THALABI:v10p305/r1.claim: He notes that the wording condemns those heedless of prayer, not those merely heedless during prayer.
THALABI:v10p305/r1.anchor: الحمد لله الذي قال: الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون ولم يقل في صلاتهم

THALABI:v10p305/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r2.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p305/r2.claim: He says the person prays for show and feels no regret when missing the prayer.
THALABI:v10p305/r2.anchor: هو الذي إن صلاها صلاها رياء وأن فاتته لم يندم

THALABI:v10p305/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v10p305/r3.claim: He says they fail to pray at the proper times and do not complete bowing and prostration.
THALABI:v10p305/r3.anchor: لا يصلونها لمواقيتها ولا يتمون ركوعها ولا سجودها

THALABI:v10p305/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p305/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v10p305/r4.claim: He also says they turn their heads back and forth while prostrating.
THALABI:v10p305/r4.anchor: إذا سجد قال برأسه هكذا وهكذا ملتفتا

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r5.claim: The warning now turns to those who pray or appear to be believers, threatening them with woe for being heedless of their prayers.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r5.anchor: daha doğrusu namaz kılıyor mü’min görünenlere

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r6.claim: Prayer should gather the heart before God, bring a kind of meeting with Him, and elicit aid and guidance for sincere service; heedlessness abandons these purposes.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r6.anchor: dinin direği ve kulların cem‘iyyet-i kalb ile huzûr-ı Hakk’a durarak bir yükselişi, likāullâha bir nevi visâli demek olan

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r7.speaker: Atâ b. Dînâr
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r7.claim: He explains that the verse condemns heedlessness away from prayer, not involuntary mistakes during prayer, which human beings cannot fully avoid.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r7.anchor: Atâ b. Dînâr’dan mervî olduğu üzere denilmiştir

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r8.claim: Heedlessness includes treating prayer as unimportant, neglecting whether or when it is performed, delaying or abandoning it without regret, praying insincerely for worldly aims, or praying publicly but not privately.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r8.anchor: kılınıp kılınmadığına aldırmamak, vaktine dikkat etmemek, geçip geçmediğine mübâlât etmeyip vaktinden tehir eylemek, terkinden müteessir olmamak

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r9.claim: Heedlessness also includes performing prayer as empty display or amusement rather than sincere worship; complete abandonment is outside the address to people who pray.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r9.anchor: Söz musallî denilenlerde olduğu için büsbütün terk bu mevzudan hâriç olmak gerektir

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r10.speaker: Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkas
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r10.claim: He reports asking the Prophet about those heedless of prayer and receiving the explanation that they delay it past its proper time.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r10.anchor: Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkas radıyallâhu anh’tan, demiştir ki: “Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’ne

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r11.speaker: Ebû Berzete’l-Eslemî
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r11.claim: He reports that the Prophet called the verse better than receiving the whole world and described people who neither expect reward from their prayer nor fear their Lord when abandoning it.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r11.anchor: Ebû Berzete’l-Eslemî radıyallâhu anh’tan, demiştir ki:

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.claim: The context includes people who perform a few prayers smugly as if religion consisted only of them, neglecting other duties such as almsgiving and help for God's servants.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r12.anchor: kıldıkları birkaç vakit namazdan dolayı mağrur olup yanılıp da din ondan ibaret imiş gibi sâir ibadet ve ubûdiyet vazifelerini yapmayanlar da dâhil olur

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly pairs prayer with zakat as foundational righteous duties after faith; some who seem devout wrongly neglect financial obligations.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r13.anchor: Kur’an’da imandan sonra sâlih amellerin esası olmak üzere namaz ve zekât beraber zikrolunagelmiştir

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.claim: Mosques are maintained by those who believe in God and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear only God.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r14.anchor: إِنَّمَا يَعْمُرُ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَلَمْ يَخْشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.claim: Prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing; people who persist in these and refuse aid have ignored prayer's admonition and meaning.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r15.anchor: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.claim: Religious pretenders who neglect prayer, show off, and withhold even small help are more astonishingly blameworthy than disbelievers who deny religion and mistreat orphans and the poor.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.anchor: namaz kılar dindar görünüp de namazlarından yanılan, mürâîlik, gösteriş yapıp

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.claim: After the address to the Prophet to see and understand, Sūrat al-Kawthar condenses the preceding suras, especially those from al-Ḍuḥā, as a final account of Muhammad's rank.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.anchor: Ve’d-Duhâ’dan beri gelen sûrelerin mazmûnu üzerinde hepsinin tetimmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.claim: After condemning failure in one's duties toward people, the surah criticizes those who fail to fulfill genuine duties of worship toward God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.anchor: Yukarıda insanlara karşı insanlık görevini yerine getirmeyenler kınanmıştı; burada ise Allah’a karşı gerçek anlamda kulluk görevlerini yerine getirmeyenler eleştirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.claim: Three faults are given among people who pray: distance from prayer's essence, ostentation in worship, and obstructing good.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.anchor: Namazlarının özünden uzak olmaları, b) İbadetlerinde halka gösteriş yapmaları, c) Hayra engel olmaları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r3.claim: Sahun literally means forgetful; some interpret it here as those who fail to pray on time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r3.anchor: sâhûn kelimesinin sözlük anlamı “unutanlar” olup bu bağlamda, “namazlarını vaktinde kılmayanlar” şeklinde yorumlayanlar bulunmuşsa da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r4.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r4.claim: Tabari takes sahun to mean people who disregard prayer and prefer other activities, a reading that also includes delaying prayer or abandoning it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r4.anchor: Taberî, bizim de meâlde esas aldığımız yorumunda sâhûn kelimesini, “namazı ciddiye almayanlar, başka şeylerle meşgul olmayı namaz kılmaya tercih edenler” şeklinde anlamanın daha isabetli olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.claim: Outward forms of worship remain essential, but equal care is due to its inner substance: faith, intention, sincerity, reverence, and piety.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r8.anchor: şekil şartları da vazgeçilmez olmakla birlikte, en az şekil kadar özen gösterilmesi gereken husus

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.claim: Intention and sincerity in worship reflect the principle of divine unity, as illustrated by the cited verses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r9.anchor: Kur’an’a göre ibadetlerde niyet ve ihlâs, tevhid ilkesinin ibadetteki yansımasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r10.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r10.claim: The Prophet describes worship as serving God as though one sees Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r10.anchor: Bunu Hz. Peygamber, “Allah’ı görüyormuşçasına ibadet etmek” şeklinde belirtmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.claim: The surah stresses that sincere worship of God and mutual aid and solidarity cannot be separated in religious devotion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.anchor: Allah’a gönülden ibadet etmekle yardımlaşma ve dayanışmanın dindarlıkta birbirinden ayrılmazlığının vurgulanmış olması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.claim: A truly believing person fulfills duties toward God and creation sincerely, does good, and enables rather than blocks its spread through social cooperation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.anchor: yardımlaşma ve dayanışmanın önünü tıkayan değil, aksine gelişip yaygınlaşmasına, bireyselliği aşarak toplumsal ve kurumsal bir yapı kazanmasına katkıda bulunan insandır

BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r2.claim: Given their disregard for orphan and poor, the conditional implication is that woe means severe punishment for these worshippers.
BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r2.anchor: الفاء لربط ما بعدها بشرط محذوف كأنه قيل إذ كان ما ذكر من عدم المبالاة باليتيم والمسكين

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies these worshippers as hypocrites who pray for show when seen, abandon prayer when alone, and withhold household loans out of spite; these loans are al-ma'un.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون قال : هم المنافقون يراءون الناس بصلاتهم اذا حضروا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r1.claim: The surah has six reported titles: al-Maʿun, Araʾayta, Araʾayta alladhi, al-Maʿun wa-l-Din wa-Araʾayta, al-Din, al-Takdhib, and al-Yatim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r1.anchor: وقال البقاعي في ( نظم الدرر ) تسمى ( سورة اليتيم ) . وهذه ستة أسماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r2.claim: Most say it is Meccan; reports from Ibn Abbas and Qatada call it Medinan, while a view attributed to Ibn Abbas makes the first three verses Meccan and the rest Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r2.anchor: وهي مكية في قول الأكثر . وروي عن ابن عباس ، وقال القرطبي عن قتادة : هي مدنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r3.speaker: هبة الله الضرير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r3.claim: The author calls the split-revelation account most plausible: the latter verses address hypocrites.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r4.claim: If Meccan, it ranks seventeenth in revelation order, after al-Takathur and before al-Kafirun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r4.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة التكاثر وقبل سورة الكافرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r5.claim: Most verse counters count six verses; al-Alusi says the Iraqi schools count six, while Ali al-Nuri al-Safaqsi reports seven in the Himsi count and six elsewhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r5.anchor: وعدت آياتها ستا عند معظم العادين . وحكى الآلوسي أن الذين عدوا آياتها ستا أهل العراق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r6.claim: The surah exposes deniers of resurrection through abuse of the weak, refusal to feed the poor, and neglect of prayer and alms without fear of God's punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p563/r6.anchor: من مقاصدها التعجيب من حال من كذبوا بالبعث وتفظيع أعمالهم من الاعتداء على الضعيف واحتقاره والإمساك عن إطعام المسكين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r2.claim: The fā explicitly links the warning to the preceding description; on a wholly Meccan reading, the same denier neglects prayer, performs it for show, and withholds aid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r2.anchor: موقع الفاء صريح في اتصال ما بعدها بما قبلها من الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r3.claim: Calling them “prayers” is mockery: they do not truly pray and are not Muslims, as in 74:43–44; naming them explicitly avoids an awkward list of six traits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r3.anchor: فوصفهم ب ( المصلين ) إذن تهكم ، والمراد عدمه ، أي الذين لا يصلون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r4.claim: The placement of wayl before the explicit noun signals punishment for all the preceding vices, as al-Kashshaf hints.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r4.anchor: إلى أن الويل ناشىء عن جميع تلك الصفات التي هو أهلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r5.claim: Ibn Wahb and Ashhab transmit from Malik the Medinan interpretation that these heedless prayers are hypocrites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r5.anchor: وروى هذا ابن وهب وأشهب عن مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r6.claim: The plural fits the generic deniers; if a particular person is intended, it generalizes the warning to others sharing neglect of prayer, ostentation, and refusal of aid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p566/r6.anchor: وجيء في هذه الصفة بصيغة الجمع لأن المراد ب { الذي يكذب بالدين }

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244#2/r1.claim: The passage concerns hypocrites who expect reward for praying in the Prophet's presence but do not fear punishment when they skip prayer, so they pray for show when he is there and leave it otherwise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244#2/r1.anchor: نزل هذا في المنافقين الذين يرجون لصلاتهم ثوابا ولا يخافون على تركها عقابا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.claim: They identify the threatened worshippers as hypocrites who pray publicly but do not pray in private.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وغيره: يعني المنافقين،

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r12.claim: The woe announced for the worshippers means punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r12.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فويل للمصلين } أي عذاب لهم

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.claim: Although Qutb leans toward a wholly Medinan setting because hypocrisy and ostentation were unfamiliar in Mecca, he allows later verses to have been appended for thematic continuity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.anchor: وإن كانت السورة كلها وحدة متماسكة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.claim: The seven short verses overturn conventional ideas of faith and disbelief and reveal the creed’s mercy and immense good for humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة الصغيرة ذات الآيات السبع القصيرة تعالج حقيقة ضخمة تكاد تبدل المفهوم السائد للإيمان والكفر

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.claim: Religion is an integrated way of life whose worship, rites, and personal and social duties purify hearts and lead people to cooperation, care, and flourishing.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.anchor: إنما هو منهج متكامل ، تتعاون عباداته وشعائره

QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r1.claim: The warning of ruin applies to people who are heedless of their prayer.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r1.anchor: إنه دعاء أو وعيد بالهلاك للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون

QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r2.claim: Those heedless worshippers are the ones who show off and withhold small acts of help.

QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r3.claim: They perform prayer but fail to establish it.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:4/r3.anchor: إنهم أولئك الذين يصلون ، ولكنهم لا يقيمون الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r1.claim: One link is that mistreating the orphan and withholding help show hypocrisy, while prayer without humility is an even clearer sign because it concerns service to the Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r1.anchor: معاملة مع المخلوق ، أما الصلاة فإنها خدمة للخالق

RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r2.claim: Another link answers the objection that prayer restrains indecency: this prayer cannot restrain evil when it consists of ostentation and inattention.
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r2.anchor: الصلاة كيف تنهاه عن هذا الفعل المنكر

RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r3.claim: A third link says orphan abuse neglects compassion for God’s creatures, and heedlessness in prayer neglects reverence for God; failing in both completes wretchedness.
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r3.anchor: وسهوه في الصلاة تقصير فيما يرجع إلى التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r4.claim: Woe is used for grave crimes, as in warnings against fraud, scribal wrongdoing, and slander.
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r4.anchor: إن هذا اللفظ إنما يستعمل عند الجريمة الشديدة

RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r5.claim: A report says each person in Hell wails according to his offense, including love of status, tribal zeal, or prayer; the listener should say, Woe to me unless God forgives me.
RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r5.anchor: كل أحد ينوح في النار بحسب جريمته

RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r1.claim: The threat covers three sins: heedlessness about prayer, ostentation, and withholding small aid; since these do not alone make a Muslim hypocrite, commentators explain why the warning is so severe.

RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r2.claim: The preferred answer limits the description to hypocritical worshippers: their extra punishment for forbidden acts and omitted duties supports al-Shafi‘i’s view that unbelievers are addressed by the subsidiary laws.

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r1.claim: The commentary points readers to earlier discussions for the possible meanings of wayl.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r1.anchor: For the possible meanings of woe

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r2.claim: The verses may refer to disbelievers' prayer at the House, elsewhere described as whistling and clapping.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r2.anchor: These verses could be seen as a reference to the prayer of the disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r3.speaker: majority of commentators
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r3.claim: The heedless gain no benefit from prayers they perform and fear no retribution when they omit them.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r3.anchor: the majority of commentators interpret them as a reference to those who, because of their heedlessness, receive no benefit from their prayers

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r4.speaker: majority of commentators
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r4.claim: Alternatively, the warning targets hypocrites who pray in public but not in private.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r4.anchor: or to the hypocrites, who pray in public, but not in private

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r5.claim: The warning can target those who miss prayer times or fail to complete the required bows and prostrations.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r5.anchor: those who fail to perform their prayers at the proper time or who do not complete the required bows and prostrations

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r6.claim: Another interpretation covers people who perform every prayer properly but lack humility, contemplation, and remembrance of God.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r6.anchor: those who perform all of the prayers properly, but fail to do so with humility, contemplation, and remembrance of God

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r7.claim: A hadith calls a delayed, hastily pecked prayer with little remembrance the prayer of a hypocrite.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r7.anchor: A ḥadīth states, “This is the prayer of the hypocrite. He sits watching the sun

STUDYQURAN:107:4/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r8.claim: The consequences of neglecting prayers are discussed at 19:59.
STUDYQURAN:107:4/r8.anchor: Regarding the implications of neglecting prayers, see 19:59c.

TAB:107:4/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:4/r1.speaker: author
TAB:107:4/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī glosses the woe as a valley flowing with Hell's pus, for hypocrites who pray without seeking God and are heedless in prayer.
TAB:107:4/r1.anchor: فالوادي الذي يسيل من صديد أهل جهنم للمنافقين الذين يصلون ، لا يريدون الله عز وجل بصلاتهم

TAB:107:4/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:4/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are hypocrites who display prayer before people, abandon it when unseen, and withhold borrowed household goods.
TAB:107:4/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : { فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون } فهم المنافقون كانوا يراؤون الناس بصلاتهم إذا حضروا

SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r1.claim: The lām is the predicate of fa-wayl and the fa marks consequence: their shameful traits lead to the threat of woe.
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r1.anchor: للمصلين } خبر لقوله: " فويل " والفاء للتسبب،أي: تسبب عن هذه الصفات الذميمة الدعاء عليهم بالويل

SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r2.claim: He links the question about the denier and the mistreatment of the orphan and poor to woe for performers of prayer who deny, neglect prayer, show off, and withhold alms.
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري بعد قوله: " كأنه قيل: أخبرني، وما تقول فيمن يكذب بالدين إلى قوله: أنعم ما يصنع

SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r3.speaker: the Shaykh
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r3.claim: The Shaykh calls it strained to replace a singular pronoun with al-musallin, a plural, and says the Qur'an should follow its apparent sense.
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r3.anchor: وأما وضعه المصلين موضع الضمير، وأن المصلين جمع؛ لأن ضمير الذي يكذب معناه الجمع فتكلف واضح

SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r4.claim: The author accuses the Shaykh of unfairly disparaging al-Zamakhshari and defends the reading as a coherent unified description with heightened threat.
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r4.anchor: وعادة شيخنا - رحمه الله - التحامل على الزمخشري حتى يجعل حسنه قبيحا. وكيف يرد ما قاله وفيه ارتباط الكلام بعضه ببعض

SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r5.claim: The apparent passage describes a group combining denial of Judgment, pushing away orphans, failing to urge feeding the poor, neglecting prayer, showing off, and withholding good.
SAMIN-DURR:107:4/r5.anchor: أن السورة كلها في وصف قوم جمعوا بين هذه الأوصاف كلها: من التكذيب بالدين ودفع اليتيم وعدم الحض على طعامه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p357/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p357/r5.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p357/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqatil say the threatened worshipers are hypocrites.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p357/r5.anchor: قوله: {فويل للمصلين (4)} قال الكلبي (3) (ومقاتل (4)) (5): يعني من المنافقين.

WAHIDI-QT:107:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:107:4/r1.claim: The prayer's heedless practitioners delay it beyond its appointed time.
WAHIDI-QT:107:4/r1.anchor: { فويل للمصلين } { الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون } غافلون يؤخرونها عن وقتها

WAHIDI-QT:107:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:107:5/r1.claim: The prayer's heedless practitioners delay it beyond its appointed time.
WAHIDI-QT:107:5/r1.anchor: { فويل للمصلين } { الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون } غافلون يؤخرونها عن وقتها

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p235#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p235#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p235#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the threatened worshippers were hypocrites who performed prayer ostentatiously when believers saw them, abandoned it when unseen, and withheld borrowed household goods.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p235#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ فويل للمصلين ﴾ الآية قال نزلت في المنافقين كانوا يراؤون المؤمنين بصلاتهم

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r1.claim: The root s-h-w here likely means the same as the later frequent term ghafla, religious heedlessness and negligence condemned also by Ephrem, according to Andrae; compare 51:11.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: der u. a. bei Ephrem verurteilten religiösen Sorglosigkeit und Nachlässigkeit entspricht

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r2.claim: For ṣallā and ṣalāh, the notes refer to the discussion under 108:2.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-5:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zu ṣallā und ṣalāh vgl. die Anmerkung zu 108:2

ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#3/r1.claim: Those heedless of prayer are unconcerned enough to miss it altogether or let its time expire, or they perform it unlike the Prophet and early Muslims, hurriedly and without reverence or attention.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#3/r1.anchor: أي غافلون غير مبالين بها حتى تفوتهم بالكلية أو يخرج وقتها أو لا يصلونها كما صلاها رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم والسلف ولكن ينقرونها نقرا ولا يخشعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r8.claim: The threatened worshippers are heedless about their prayers, specifically neglecting their appointed times.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r8.anchor: {فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون} [أي: عن مواقيتها غافلون]

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.claim: Woe is for worshippers who are inattentive to their prayers, heedless and unconcerned about them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.anchor: ساهون } أي غافلون غير مبالين بها

BINTSHATI:v2p188/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p188/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p188/r1.claim: The author previously surveyed the Qur'anic use of wayl when discussing the opening of al-Humaza.
BINTSHATI:v2p188/r1.anchor: سبق الحديث عن لفظ "ويل" واستقراء الاستعمال القرآني له، في تفسير آية الهمزة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.claim: Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.anchor: مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث ، فإنه يجزئ المكذب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.claim: Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostentation and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.anchor: إن هذه كلها من شأن المكذب بالحساب والجزاء لأن نفع البعد عنها إنما يكون إذ ذاك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r1.claim: After faults toward people, the text turns to faults toward God: both reveal a ruined heart and invite divine displeasure, showing how destructive sins are.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r1.anchor: وأن المعاصي شؤم مهلك , تنفيرا عنها وتحذيرا منها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r2.claim: The threat begins with wa'il, the strongest expression of humiliation, then targets people characterized by heedlessness of prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r2.anchor: فسبب عنه قوله معبرا بأعظم ما يدل على الإهانة : { فويل }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r3.claim: The plural 'those who pray' generalizes the warning to the whole class: whoever scorns the weak may neglect what is unseen, and one who abandons prayer is still more careless about other duties.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r3.anchor: وكان من أضاع الصلاة كان لما سواها أضيع , وكان من باشرها ربما ظن النجاة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r4.claim: A description rather than a verb ties the threat to a persistent trait; the intended targets are accountable people liable to prayer, not simply anyone presently performing it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r4.anchor: علم أن المقصود إنما هو من كان مكلفا بالصلاة لأن من كان متلبسا بها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r5.claim: A prophetic report says God does not accept the prayer of a menstruating woman unless she wears a head covering, supporting the reference to those obligated to pray.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r5.anchor: مثل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا يقبل الله صلاة حائض إلا بخمار )

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the inattentive worshippers as hypocrites: they pray ostentatiously in public, abandon prayer in private, and withhold loaned household items; this is al-maʿun.
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون} قال: هم المنافقون يراؤون الناس بصلاتهم إذا حضروا

TAB:107:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:5/r1.speaker: author
TAB:107:5/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains woe as a valley of Hell’s pus for hypocrites who pray without intending God and are heedless while praying.
TAB:107:5/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره :  فالوادي الذي يسيل من صديد أهل جهنم للمنافقين الذين يصلون ،

BURHAN:v1p38/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p38/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p38/r8.claim: Al-Kawthar’s command to pray answers al-Māʿūn’s criticism of abandoning prayer, while praying “to your Lord” answers ostentation by directing worship to God’s approval.
BURHAN:v1p38/r8.anchor: وفى مقابلة ترك الصلاة فصل أى دم عليها وفى مقابلة الرياء ﴿ لربك ﴾ أى لرضاه

BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman says Surat al-Maun is Meccan except from فويل للمصلين through its end, which is Medinan.
BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1.anchor: سورة ﴿ أرأيت ﴾ مكية إلا قوله ﴿ فويل للمصلين ﴾ إلى آخرها فإنها مدنية كذا قال مقاتل بن سليمان

ITQAN:v3p297/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.claim: Al-Kawthar counters al-Ma'un's four traits: abundant giving opposes miserliness, prayer opposes neglect, worship for God opposes showing off, and sacrifice meat is charity opposing withholding small kindnesses.
ITQAN:v3p297/r2.anchor: لأن السابقة وصف الله فيها المنافق بأربعة أمور البخل وترك الصلاة والرياء فيها ومنع الزكاة

ITQAN:v1p227/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p227/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p227/r3.claim: Stopping at “woe to those who pray” is among the most abhorrent stops because the unfinished phrase suggests a false meaning.
ITQAN:v1p227/r3.anchor: وأقبح منه نحو ﴿ إن الله لا يستحيي ﴾ ﴿ فويل للمصلين ﴾ ﴿ لا تقربوا الصلاة ﴾

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.claim: The preposition عن makes the warning concern heedlessness of prayer's purpose: standing before God, restraining wrongdoing, cultivating humility, and prompting care for orphans and the poor.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r1.anchor: فنرى النذير بالويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون غافلون عن كونها قياما بين يدي الخالق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.claim: This is not forgetfulness during prayer, abandoning prayer or its time, or fidgeting and yawning; some pray on time and feign humility for an audience or benefit, turning prayer into ostentation and formal hypocrisy.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r2.anchor: ليس السهو عن الصلاة إذن سهوا فيها ولا تركا لها أو ترك وقتها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati rejects interpreting sahūn as ordinary forgetfulness during prayer; the preposition ʿan points away from prayer rather than to a lapse within it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r2.anchor: نستبعد قول من تأولوا السهو عن الصلاة في الآية، بأنه سهو في الصلاة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r3.claim: Incidental forgetfulness in prayer is not a sin or wrong; it can be repaired by prostration for forgetfulness or by sunnah and voluntary prayers, which is why it cannot be the condemned lapse.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r3.anchor: فليس السهو فيها بخطيئة أو منكر، وكل مؤمن عرضة لأن يسهو في صلاته

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r4.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says the condemned are heedless of prayer, distracted from it, and thereby sometimes neglect prayer itself or its time; Bint al-Shati says she is not persuaded by this reading.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r4.anchor: ما ذهب إليه الإمام الطبري في قوله: "وأوْلى الأقوال عندي بالصواب، أنهم ساهون لاهون يتغافلون عنها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī adds that they may pray unlike the Prophet and early Muslims, pecking through the prayer without humility or avoiding disliked acts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p202/r5.anchor: ما أضافه الزمخشري: أو لا يصلونها كما صلاها رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والسلف. ولكن ينقرونها نقرا

NASHR:v1p229/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p229/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p229/r4.claim: Pausing at “woe to those who pray” distorts the sense and is prohibited except when an unavoidable interruption, such as breathlessness, forces it.
NASHR:v1p229/r4.anchor: وفويل للمصلين) فالوقف على ذلك كله لا يجوز إلا اضطرارا لانقطاع النفس

NASHR:v2p203/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p203/r1.speaker: أهل الأداء
NASHR:v2p203/r1.claim: Teachers forbid stopping between a genitive annexation and its governing noun; they rejected the defense that such a written break merely marked a hypothetical pause.
NASHR:v2p203/r1.anchor: إنما ذلك لو وقع الوقف لكان هذا. وأما أن يجوز قطع المضاف من المضاف إليه فلا

NASHR:v2p203/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p203/r2.speaker: أهل الأداء
NASHR:v2p203/r2.claim: The sixth rule requires a reader to finish the second reciter's reading to the end of the verse before restoring anything omitted from the first, avoiding an unmarked splice of two readers.
NASHR:v2p203/r2.anchor: وأما إتمام الخلف إلى آخره فلا يجوز عندهم إذا قرأ القارئ ثم قرأ بعده القارئ الآخر

NASHR:v2p203/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p203/r3.speaker: القيجاطي
NASHR:v2p203/r3.claim: The seventh rule's preferred order is Warsh before Qālūn and Qunbul before al-Bazzī; teachers tolerate other orders, though following the authors' order is best.
NASHR:v2p203/r3.anchor: وهو أن يبدأ بورش قبل قالون وبقنبل قبل البزي بحسب ترتيبهم فهذا أسهل الأوجه السبعة

NASHR:v2p203/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p203/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p203/r4.claim: The author says the proposed rules remain insufficient: stopping at “woe to those who pray” or beginning a fragment about believing in God can mislead; he also reports a teacher rebuking someone who stopped after “the hands of Abū Lahab” merely to display madd lengths.
NASHR:v2p203/r4.anchor: وكذلك في الاقتصار على الستة الباقية إذ ليست وافية بالقصد تجنب ما لا يليق مما يوهم غير المعنى المراد

NASHR:v2p203/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p203/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p203/r6.claim: Four conditions are essential for combining readings: observe stopping and starting, perform well, and avoid تركيب (mixing readings into an invalid composite).
NASHR:v2p203/r6.anchor: أن الذي يشترط على جامعي القراءات أربعة شروط لا بد منها، وهي رعاية الوقف

NASHR:v2p203/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p203/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p203/r7.claim: A fixed reader order is unnecessary; the skilled reader may begin with any reader but should resume that same reader after a pause, which better avoids mixing and shows command.
NASHR:v2p203/r7.anchor: لا يلتزم تقديم شخص بعينه ولكن من إذا وقف على وجه لقارئ ابتدأ لذلك القارئ

NASHR:v2p203/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p203/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p203/r8.claim: Some combine readings in graduated order: move from shorter to longer madd, or from longer to shorter, and likewise sequence degrees of imālah and hamza treatment.
NASHR:v2p203/r8.anchor: وبعضهم كان يراعي في الجمع نوعا آخر، وهو التناسب فكان إذا ابتدأ مثلا بالقصر أتى بالمرتبة التي فوقه

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī proposes coordinating fa-dhālika with alladhī yukadhdhib, deleting arayta’s second object and using the following woe as its indication.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : بعد أن قدم فيما نقلناه من كلامه ما يدل على أن { فذلك الذي يدع } في موضع رفع ،   قال : وطريقة أخرى

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads “woe to the praying” as “woe to them”: their description replaces the pronoun because they deny requital, neglect prayer, show off, and do not purify their wealth.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r7.anchor: ثم قال : { فويل للمصلين } : أي إذا علم أنه مسيء

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.claim: Treating plural al-muṣallīn as a substitute for the singular alladhī by construing it generically is forced; the Qurʾān should follow the apparent syntax.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.anchor: لأن ضمير الذي يكذب معناه الجمع ،   فتكلف واضح ولا ينبغي أن يحمل القرآن إلا على ما اقتضاه ظاهر التركيب

ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r1.claim: After naming denial of requital as the root of unbelief, the sūra turns to its consequence concerning the Creator: worship through prayer.
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر أولا عمود الكفر ،   وهو التكذيب بالدين ،   ذكر ما يترتب عليه مما يتعلق بالخالق ،   وهو عبادته بالصلاة ،   فقال : { فويل للمصلين }

ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r2.claim: The apparent reading is that these praying people are other than the person previously described.
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن المصلين هم غير المذكور

ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r3.claim: One view identifies the praying person as the orphan-pusher who does not encourage feeding the poor, with each vice arising from denial of requital.
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو داع اليتيم غير الحاض ،   وأن كلا من الأوصاف الذميمة ناشىء عن التكذيب بالدين

ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r4.claim: The praying people here are, God knows best, hypocrites; their prayer is established only as the outward postures they perform.
ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r4.anchor: فالمصلون هنا ،   والله أعلم ،   هم المنافقون ،   ثبت لهم الصلاة ،   وهي الهيئات التي يفعلونها

ALUSI:107:4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:4/r1.claim: The threat concerns worshippers indifferent to prayer: they may omit it altogether or let its time expire.
ALUSI:107:4/r1.anchor: أي غافلون غير مبالين بها حتى تفوتهم بالكلية أو يخرج وقتها

ALUSI:107:5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:5/r1.claim: The threat concerns worshippers indifferent to prayer: they may omit it altogether or let its time expire.
ALUSI:107:5/r1.anchor: أي غافلون غير مبالين بها حتى تفوتهم بالكلية أو يخرج وقتها

ALUSI:107:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r11.claim: The fāʾ in fa-wayl is consequential: the discourse escalates from orphan-pushing to prayer-neglect, ostentation, and withholding zakāt or customary loans, increasingly exposing denial of religion.
ALUSI:107:7/r11.anchor: جزائية والكلام ترق من ذلك المعرف إلى معرف أقوى

ALUSI:107:7/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r16.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI:107:7/r16.claim: The Kashf author says that if the orphan-pusher is a named individual, treating the later prayer-neglect and ostentation as further identifying labels is ill-fitting; those clauses work as a digression prompted by the orphan-pushing description.
ALUSI:107:7/r16.anchor: قال «صاحب الكشف » غير ملائم بل يكون شبه استطراد

ALUSI:107:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's main concern is denial of religion, using orphan-abuse as its identifying sign and the later vices to press the question whether such conduct is good or evil, like the rebuke in 5:91.
ALUSI:107:7/r17.anchor: فكأنه قيل أخبرني ما تقول فيمن يكذبون بالدين وفيمن يؤذون اليتيم

ALUSI:107:7/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r18.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:107:7/r18.claim: Some make the fāʾ causal from the preceding coordination, requiring the worshippers and deniers to be one group; they are then identified as hypocrites, a reading reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Mālik, and supported by the ostentation clause.
ALUSI:107:7/r18.anchor: وجعل بعضهم الفاء في فويل على العطف المذكور للسببية وهذا الوجه يقتضي اتحاد المصلين والمكذبين

ALUSI:107:7/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r19.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والإمام مالك
ALUSI:107:7/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Imām Mālik are reported to identify the worshippers as hypocrites; al-Baḥr cites the ostentation description as evidence.
ALUSI:107:7/r19.anchor: بل روى إطلاق القول بأنهم المرادون عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والإمام مالك

ALUSI:107:7/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r20.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r20.claim: On the unified-group reading, the worshippers could be all legally accountable people, even non-hypocrite disbelievers, and heedlessness could mean total abandonment of prayer, entailing that disbelievers are obligated by legal branches.
ALUSI:107:7/r20.anchor: ويصح أن يراد بالمصلين على الاتحاد المكلفون بالصلاة ولو كفاراً غير منافقين

ALUSI:107:7/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r21.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:107:7/r21.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that causal coordination making both clauses one group yields an awkward construction; the demonstrative is unnecessary and less natural than a relative clause or direct coordination.
ALUSI:107:7/r21.anchor: واعترض أبو حيان ذلك الوجه بأن التركيب عليه تركيب غريب

ALUSI:107:7/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r22.claim: Another view treats the demonstrative as an emphatic insertion pointing to the person's extreme distance in evil and corruption.
ALUSI:107:7/r22.anchor: وقيل إن اسم الإشارة هنا مقحم للإشارة إلى بعد المنزلة في الشر والفساد

ALUSI:107:7/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r23.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r23.claim: A further analysis coordinates two entities and asks whether the deniers and orphan-pushers are in a good or bad state; al-Kashf objects that the pronoun cannot naturally refer to both groups and be replaced by worshippers.
ALUSI:107:7/r23.anchor: وجوز أيضاً أن يكون العطف عطف ذات على ذات فالاستخبار عن حال المكذبين وحال الداعين

BAYDAWI:107:7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:7/r5.claim: Calling them worshippers rather than using a pronoun highlights their bad treatment of both Creator and creatures.
BAYDAWI:107:7/r5.anchor: وإنما وضع المصلين موضع الضمير للدلالة على سوء معاملتهم مع الخالق والخلق

BIQAI:107:4/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:4/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:4/r1.claim: Cruelty toward creatures is followed by the person's state toward the Creator; both reveal a ruined heart, incur divine displeasure, and warn that sins destroy.
BIQAI:107:4/r1.anchor: ولما كان هذا حاله مع الخلائق ، أتبعه حاله مع الخالق إعلاماً بأن كلاًّ منهما دالّ على خراب القلب وموجب لمقت الرب

BIQAI:107:4/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:4/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:4/r2.claim: The wording uses the strongest expression of humiliation; the implied original is singular “to him,” matching the generic singular denier.
BIQAI:107:4/r2.anchor: وكان المراد ب  "  الذي  "  الجنس الصالح للواحد وما فوقه

BIQAI:107:4/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:4/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:4/r3.claim: The plural warns that despising the weak makes one disregard what is absent; one who neglects prayer is even more careless about other duties.
BIQAI:107:4/r3.anchor: وكان من يستهين بالضعيف لضعفه يعرض عما لا يراه ولا يحسه لغيبته ، وكان من أضاع الصلاة كان لما سواها أضيع

BIQAI:107:4/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:4/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:4/r4.claim: The descriptive plural generalizes the warning and blocks complacency: someone may perform prayer yet suppose himself safe although showing off or another nullifier ruins the deed.
BIQAI:107:4/r4.anchor: وكان من باشرها ربما ظن النجاة ولو كانت مباشرته لها على وجه الرياء أو غيره من الأمور المحيطة للعمل ، عبر بالوصف تعميماً وتعليقاً للحكم به

DURR:107:4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:107:4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies these inattentive worshippers as hypocrites: they pray for show when seen, leave prayer when alone, and out of spite withhold borrowed goods, which are al-māʿūn.
DURR:107:4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس { فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون } قال : هم المنافقون يراؤون الناس بصلاتهم إذا حضروا

IBNASHUR:107:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:4/r1.claim: The initial fa explicitly makes the following statement a consequence of, and connected to, the preceding discourse.
IBNASHUR:107:4/r1.anchor: موقع الفاء صريح في اتصال ما بعدها بما قبلها

IBNASHUR:107:4/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:4/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:4/r2.claim: If the whole sura is Meccan, the worshipers are the same class as those who deny judgment, repel the orphan, and fail to urge feeding the poor.
IBNASHUR:107:4/r2.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالمصلين عين المراد بالذي يكذب بالدين

IBNASHUR:107:4/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:4/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:4/r3.claim: Calling them worshipers replaces a pronoun with another listed trait, avoiding a monotonous run of six parallel traits; placing woe here shows all their traits occasion it, as al-Kashshaf hints.
IBNASHUR:107:4/r3.anchor: إظهار في مقام الإضمار كأنه قيل : فويل له

IBNASHUR:107:4/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:4/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:4/r4.claim: On the Meccan reading, calling them worshipers is mockery: it means people who do not pray and are not Muslims, confirmed by the next description.

IBNASHUR:107:4/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:4/r5.speaker: ابن وهب وأشهب عن مالك
IBNASHUR:107:4/r5.claim: Ibn Wahb and Ashhab transmit from Malik the view that if the sura, or these verses, are Medinan, the inattentive worshipers are hypocrites; the fa links this passage to what precedes.
IBNASHUR:107:4/r5.anchor: وروى هذا ابن وهب وأشهب عن مالك

IBNASHUR:107:4/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:4/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:4/r6.claim: The plural suits the apparent reading that the denier is a class; if an earlier view meant one specific person, the plural generalizes to include him among others with these traits.
IBNASHUR:107:4/r6.anchor: وجيء في هذه الصفة بصيغة الجمع لأن المراد ب { الذي يكذب بالدين }

IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.speaker: هبة الله بن سلامة
IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.claim: Hibat Allah ibn Salama reports in al-Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh that these three verses were revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.
IBNASHUR:107:7/r3.anchor: وحكى هبة الله بن سلامة في كتاب « الناسخ والمنسوخ »

IBNASHUR:107:7/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:7/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:7/r10.claim: The author proposes a general principle: when revelation is attached to an earlier passage, its wording is shaped to fit that context, which explains the consequential fa.
IBNASHUR:107:7/r10.anchor: إذا أراد الله إنزال شيء من القرآن ملحقاً بشيء قبله

IBNATIYYA:107:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:4/r1.claim: A report places the revelation among people compelled into Islam in Mecca who were not firm, then succumbed to persecution and treated Muslims harshly; some prayed with them at times out of caution or confusion.
IBNATIYYA:107:4/r1.anchor: ويروى أن هذه السورة نزلت في بعض المضطرين في الإسلام بمكة الذين لم يحققوا فيه

IBNATIYYA:107:4/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:4/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA:107:4/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abu Sufyan slaughtered a camel each week; when an orphan came, Abu Sufyan struck him with a stick, and the sura was revealed about him.
IBNATIYYA:107:4/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج : كان أبو سفيان ينحر كل أسبوع جزوراً فجاءه يتيم ، فقرعه بعصا فنزلت السورة فيه

IBNATIYYA:107:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:5/r1.claim: A report places the revelation among people compelled into Islam in Mecca who were not firm, then succumbed to persecution and treated Muslims harshly; some prayed with them at times out of caution or confusion.
IBNATIYYA:107:5/r1.anchor: ويروى أن هذه السورة نزلت في بعض المضطرين في الإسلام بمكة الذين لم يحققوا فيه

IBNATIYYA:107:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:5/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA:107:5/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abu Sufyan slaughtered a camel each week; when an orphan came, Abu Sufyan struck him with a stick, and the sura was revealed about him.
IBNATIYYA:107:5/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج : كان أبو سفيان ينحر كل أسبوع جزوراً فجاءه يتيم ، فقرعه بعصا فنزلت السورة فيه

IBNKATHIR:107:4/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:107:4/r1.claim: The verse means those committed to prayer who are nevertheless heedless of it.
IBNKATHIR:107:4/r1.anchor: أي : الذين هم من أهل الصلاة وقد التزموا بها ، ثم هم عنها ساهون

IBNKATHIR:107:5/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:107:5/r1.claim: The verse means those committed to prayer who are nevertheless heedless of it.
IBNKATHIR:107:5/r1.anchor: أي : الذين هم من أهل الصلاة وقد التزموا بها ، ثم هم عنها ساهون

KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.claim: The preceding warning powerfully shows that sin signals weak faith and loose certainty; the text then adds a warning of woe for those who pray.
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.anchor: وما أبلغه في التحذير من المعصية ،   وأنها جديرة بأن يستدل بها

KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.claim: Another syntax coordinates fa-dhālika with the denier, as a noun or description; the answer to “Have you seen?” is omitted and indicated by what follows, and the plural denotes the generic singular.
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.anchor: وطريقة أخرى : أن يكون { فَذَلِكَ } عطفاً على { الذي يُكَذّبُ }

MAWARDI:107:4/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:4/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:107:4/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the warning implicitly targets a hypocrite who hopes for no reward when praying on time and fears no punishment when praying outside its time.
MAWARDI:107:4/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه المنافق ، إن صلاها لوقتها لم يرج ثوابها ، وإن صلاها لغير وقتها لم يخش عقابها ، قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI:107:4/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:4/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:4/r2.claim: Alternatively, the omitted qualification is supplied explicitly by the connected phrase that follows: “those who are heedless of their prayer.”
MAWARDI:107:4/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن إضماره ظاهر متصل به ، وهو قوله تعالى : { الذين هم } الآية .

NASAFI:107:4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:4/r1.claim: The warning continues by specifying the worshippers meant: those heedless of prayer, who show off and withhold alms or useful aid.
NASAFI:107:4/r1.anchor: { فَوَيْلٌ لّلْمُصَلّينَ الذين هُمْ عَن صلاتهم سَاهُونَ الذين هُمْ يُرَاءونَ

NASAFI:107:4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:4/r2.claim: One explanation identifies hypocrites: they avoid private prayer because they do not believe it obligatory, but pray publicly to show off.
NASAFI:107:4/r2.anchor: يعني بهذا المنافقين لا يصلونها سراً ؛ لأنهم لا يعتقدون وجوبها

NASAFI:107:4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:4/r3.claim: Another description is hypocrites who outwardly count themselves among worshippers but neglect prayer, seek neither nearness nor fulfillment of duty, go through motions mindlessly, display worship, and withhold alms and useful things.
NASAFI:107:4/r3.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة

NASAFI:107:4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:4/r6.claim: Riyāʾ is a reciprocal form from showing: the performer displays his deed to people, who respond with praise and admiration.
NASAFI:107:4/r6.anchor: والمراءاة مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يرائي الناس عمله

NASAFI:107:4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:4/r7.claim: Displaying obligatory worship is not showing off because it should be public; concealing voluntary worship is better, unless it is displayed to encourage imitation, which is good.
NASAFI:107:4/r7.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائياً بإظهار الفرائض

QURTUBI:107:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:4/r1.claim: Wayl means punishment; Qurṭubī notes that this has been explained in several earlier passages.
QURTUBI:107:4/r1.anchor: أي عذاب لهم .   وقد تقدم في غير موضع

RAZI:107:4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r1.claim: The transition from mistreating orphans and withholding food to prayer contrasts dealings with creatures against service to the Creator: prayer without humility is an even clearer sign of hypocrisy.
RAZI:107:4/r1.anchor: لأن الإيذاء والمنع من النفع معاملة مع المخلوق ، أما الصلاة فإنها خدمة للخالق

RAZI:107:4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r2.claim: Mention of orphan abuse and failure to urge feeding prompts the question whether prayer prevents wrongdoing; the answer is that ostentation and heedlessness make such prayer itself corrupt.
RAZI:107:4/r2.anchor: أليس إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ؟ فقال له : الصلاة كيف تنهاه عن هذا الفعل المنكر

RAZI:107:4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r3.claim: Neglect of compassion toward God’s creatures and neglect of reverence toward God complete the person’s misery, hence the warning.
RAZI:107:4/r3.anchor: تقصير فيما يرجع إلى الشفقة على خلق الله ، وسهوه في الصلاة تقصير

RAZI:107:4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r4.claim: Wayl is used for a grave crime, as in warnings in 83:1, 2:79, and 104:1.
RAZI:107:4/r4.anchor: إن هذا اللفظ إنما يستعمل عند الجريمة الشديدة كقوله : { ويل للمطففين }

RAZI:107:4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r5.claim: A report says each person in Hell laments according to his crime—status-seeking, tribal zeal, or prayer—so one should say on hearing the verse, “Woe to me if God does not forgive me.”
RAZI:107:4/r5.anchor: ويروى أن كل أحد ينوح في النار بحسب جريمته ، فقائل يقول : ويلي من حب الشرف
